title: Sparse vectors and cosine similarity
instructions:
Implement two cooperating modules. `sparse_vector.py` defines `SparseVector`; `vector_math.py` defines `dot`, `magnitude`, and `cosine_similarity` and imports `SparseVector`. Numeric values/scalars are finite real numbers, not booleans. Dimensions and indices are integers, not booleans. No external numerical libraries.
`SparseVector(dimension, entries=None)` takes a nonnegative dimension and an optional dict from index to value. Negative dimension raises `ValueError`. Every supplied index must satisfy 0 <= index < dimension, even for zero-valued entries, else `IndexError`. Copy entries, convert retained values to float, and omit all exact zeros. Expose read-only-by-convention attribute `dimension` (callers do not assign it).
- `vector[index] -> float`: return the value, or 0.0 for a missing in-range index; out-of-range indices raise `IndexError` (no negative indexing).
- `to_dict() -> dict[int, float]`: detached mapping of nonzero entries.
- `add(other) -> SparseVector`: elementwise addition, requiring equal dimensions or `ValueError`. Omit exact cancellations. Return a new vector and leave both inputs unchanged.
- `scale(factor) -> SparseVector`: return a new scaled vector, omitting exact zeros; leave input unchanged.
`vector_math.py` functions:
- `dot(left, right) -> float`: sum of products at matching indices. Different dimensions raise `ValueError`, including empty vectors.
- `magnitude(vector) -> float`: Euclidean length (square root of sum of squares).
- `cosine_similarity(left, right) -> float`: dot product divided by both magnitudes; return 0.0 if either magnitude is zero. Check equal dimensions first, otherwise `ValueError` even when a vector is zero.
Dimension zero is valid. Storage and computations must iterate stored entries, not all coordinates; support dimension 10**9 with a handful of entries. Floating results are compared approximately where appropriate. Intermediate arithmetic in tests stays finite.

## Files
- `sparse_vector.py`
- `vector_math.py`
